metadata.title: Artificial Intelligence in Education: Computer-Assisted Learning and AI-guided Tutors

extraction.outcome_summary: The article reviewed causal evidence on computer-assisted learning (CAL) and AI-guided tutoring, emphasizing that learning gains—especially in mathematics—depend on pedagogical design, teacher support, and implementation fidelity. Using Italy-focused evidence, it combined PISA 2022 school-questionnaire indicators on educational and digital resource shortages with an econometric analysis of regional Google Trends search intensity for ChatGPT as a proxy for AI adoption. The findings indicated persistent territorial and school-level digital divides, with lower adoption/search intensity in disadvantaged and smaller/southern regions, alongside some convergence over time. Overall, the paper argued that equitable benefits from AI in education require targeted investment and inclusive governance rather than technology access alone.
